jurisdiction.name: United Republic of Tanzania
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Tanzania governs AI mainly through the Personal Data Protection Act 2022 and its 2023 regulations, which set rules on decisions made solely by automated processing and require impact assessments for profiling and algorithmic decisions, and through the Ministry of Health's 2022 policy framework for AI in the health sector. The ICT ministry published a draft National AI Strategy Framework and draft Guidelines for the Secure and Ethical Use of AI in 2025; neither had been finalised by October 2026. There is no AI law or AI bill.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on official sites. The education ministry's document library and the standards bureau's catalogue could not be accessed, so the 2025 national guidelines on AI in education and a draft national AI risk management standard are tracked as leads. As a country of over 20 million people with few records, Tanzania is marked for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.summary: Draft national AI strategy framework from the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, aligned with Tanzania Development Vision 2050 and the Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034. It sets a vision, guiding principles and eight pillars (AI infrastructure; AI governance; skills and talent; innovation, research and entrepreneurship; inclusion and accessibility; data governance; partnership and collaboration; AI-powered transformation of production and service sectors). It proposes a Tanzania AI Observatory with a governance structure, an AI risk-management process and a monitoring, evaluation, learning and adaptation (MELA) framework.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Tanzania's first national AI strategy (draft); anchors the planned AI governance arrangements and the companion AI guidelines.

instruments.summary: Draft national guidelines from the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology for public and private stakeholders that develop, deploy or adopt AI. They set eight AI principles (valid and reliable, safe, managed bias, resilient, transparency, accountability, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced) and ten ethical-practice steps for entities (code of ethics, diverse training data, monitoring, ethical reviews, staff education, risk anticipation). They add expectations on transparency, explainability, human oversight and telling users when they are interacting with an AI system.

instruments.english_title: Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence in Tanzania Health Sector
instruments.current_status: Published by the Ministry of Health (cover dated February 2022); cited in the 2025 draft National AI Strategy Framework as an existing sector instrument. No later revision found.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Health framework setting out the processes, technologies, capabilities, stakeholders, principles and recommendations to guide the implementation and use of AI in the health sector, building on the existing digital health and data landscape. It reviews AI pilots and the role of the Centre for Digital Health, and lists what is needed: a shared vision, an enabling policy environment, leadership and coordination, quality assurance and oversight, ethical safeguards, capacity building and a review of related rules such as TMDA medical-device policies. It is meant to be the basis for future national health AI policies and regulatory mechanisms.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First sectoral AI governance document in Tanzania (health).

instruments.official_title: Sheria ya Ulinzi wa Taarifa Binafsi, 2022
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 11 of 2022, Cap. 44)
instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament of the United Republic of Tanzania
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 May 2023 (GN No. 326 of 2023). Enacted in Swahili (Act No. 11 of 2022, Act Supplement of 2 December 2022); an official English version was published by the Attorney General as GN No. 395B of 13 June 2023 (Chapter 44) and is on the PDPC website. Applies to Mainland Tanzania and to union matters in Zanzibar.
instruments.summary: Tanzania's data protection law, which sets principles for collecting and processing personal data, requires registration of data controllers and processors, and establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission. Section 36 lets a data subject require that decisions significantly affecting them are not based solely on automated processing; where they are, the controller must notify the data subject, who may ask for reconsideration (exceptions for contracts, written law or explicit consent). Section 33 gives a right to be told the logic of solely automated decisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main binding rule on automated decision-making and AI training/use of personal data.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): Swahili Act Supplement No. 11 (Gazette No. 45 Vol. 103, 2 December 2022) read via pdftotext from the MICIT acts page; official English version (GN No. 395B of 13 June 2023, Chapter 44) read from https://pdpc.go.tz/documents/3/PERSONAL_DATA_PROTECTION_ACT_2022.pdf, which gives the commencement date 1 May 2023 (GN No. 326 of 2023)

instruments.official_title: The Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023
instruments.english_title: The Personal Data Protection (Personal Data Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023
instruments.issuing_authority: Minister responsible for communication (Ministry of Communication and Information Technology)
instruments.current_status: Official English version published as GN No. 449C on 4 July 2023 under section 84(4) of the Interpretation of Laws Act; the Swahili original was not located online. Made by the Minister responsible for communication under section 64 of the Act (regulation 2 definition); effective date not stated in the version read.
instruments.summary: Regulations under the Personal Data Protection Act setting procedures for collecting and processing personal data. Regulation 19 requires controllers and processors to notify data subjects in writing when a decision significantly affecting them is based solely on automated processing, and gives a right to reject such use. Regulation 33 requires a data protection impact assessment before automated decision-making with significant legal effect that uses profiling or algorithmic means, and the privacy-by-design rules call for human intervention to minimise biases created by automated decision-making.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding algorithmic-decision notice and impact-assessment duties.
